strings: In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan guides the Church of the Holy Light from the Hall of Mysteries. He teaches young priests, helps them deepen their mastery of the Light, and keeps spiritual ties between Ironforge, Stormwind, and distant allies.
Shepherd of the Hall of Mysteries

High Priest Rohan paces the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward as the Church of the Holy Light’s highest-ranking representative in the city. Dwarves once honored the titans, yet their priests have embraced the Light’s wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan patiently teaches young acolytes to channel holy magic and steel their minds against despair.

After priests under his care master the fundamentals, Rohan sends them abroad to learn from other traditions. Human and dwarven students go to High Priestess Laurena in Stormwind City. Night elf disciples travel to Priestess Alathea at Darnassus’s Temple of the Moon to study mysteries such as Elune’s Grace. Rohan also sends healers to aid the Cenarion Circle’s druids in distant Azshara, wherever hardship calls.

Rohan keeps sacred relics for the Alliance priesthood and paladin brotherhoods. One is a blessed exorcism censer, used for years to cleanse vile spirits. When the Order of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker need it for their knights’ holy calling, Rohan lends it freely. He asks only for charitable alms to replenish Ironforge’s dwindling food reserves for the needy.

Highlord Demitrian is a solitary human hermit dwelling amidst the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus. Describing himself as a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan, he possesses the esoteric knowledge required to wake the slumbering elemental lord. Adventurers bearing ancient elemental bindings seek him out to unlock the power of the Windseeker.

Found lingering at an abandoned encampment in the Crystal Vale, Demitrian appears out of place in the desolate wastes of Silithus. Though he is tied to the Twilight's Hammer whose ravaged camp he haunts, Demitrian acts above all as a herald for Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He treats visitors with aloof indifference unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

Demitrian's purpose is tied entirely to Thunderaan's resurrection. Should an adventurer present him with the Bindings of the Windseeker—relics torn from fire elementals within the Molten Core—Demitrian provides the Vessel of Rebirth. He demands rare elemental reagents, including vast quantities of enchanted elementium and the essence of the Firelord, to reconstitute his prince's physical form.

Demitrian's ritual brings Prince Thunderaan into the Crystal Vale, where adventurers must face the restored Windseeker in battle. Once they vanquish the elemental lord, they recover the Dormant Wind Kissed Blade and bring it to the terrified Demitrian, who awakens Thunderfury in exchange.

Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics. His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades.

Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the hounds guarding the Library wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb.

Loksey is not the only beast handler in his family serving the cause. His brother, Huntsman Leopold, serves as the Scarlet Crusade's envoy to the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope Chapel. Leopold holds a low opinion of his brother, privately asserting that Loksey can barely manage his own hounds, let alone represent the order in high-stakes diplomacy. Despite Leopold's scorn, Loksey remains a key officer within the Monastery's inner hierarchy.

Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself.

Adventurers who bring Mathredis the proper tomes—such as the Librams of Constitution, Resilience, Rumination, Tenacity, or Voracity—along with rare reagents will find him eager to trade his craft. The process binds volatile magical reagents directly to the text, concentrating their essence into an arcanum that can permanently enchant headwear or leg armor. So long as adventurers supply the components, Mathredis receives both payment and the ambient arcane sustenance he desperately craves.
Mathredis Firestar is a blood elf mage stationed at the neutral outpost of Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He is an arcanist capable of forging Lesser Arcanums to enchant armor.

In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides Alliance druids from the Cenarion Enclave. Once Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he helps young druids face spiritual trials, learn shapeshifting, and serve across Kalimdor.

In Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave, Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides Alliance druids through their first rites. A respected elder of the Cenarion Circle, he sends initiates to commune with Moonglade and judges whether they are ready to take animal forms. Mathrengyl remembers his own bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit. He asks each initiate to test their spirit against Lunaclaw, the sacred moonkin, before entering the path of the Druid of the Claw.

For many years, Mathrengyl has served as Fandral Staghelm's second, tending the Cenarion Circle's daily affairs and finding recruits for the Archdruid's plans. When Fandral sought great stores of morrowgrain, Mathrengyl arranged for returning adventurers to gather it. In private, he admitted unease about the plant's unnatural essence. He also coordinates Alliance responses to calls from Moonglade and handles the Circle's delicate politics while Fandral turns his attention to southern Kalimdor.

Mathrengyl thinks more openly than Fandral Staghelm, whose pride and disdain for other races are well known. Relics from Mulgris Deepriver reached Darnassus after the druid died fighting the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands. Mathrengyl was moved to learn that the investigator was a tauren. The Cenarion Circle shares a mission, he reflected, and tauren may not have strayed as far from Cenarius's teachings as Fandral claims.
